Subject: RFP question: preservation & handoff procedures (Ref: ACME-RFP-1337)

Hi Kimberly,

Following up on section 4.2 of our RFP (evidence & legal holds): can you provide a concise description of Redwood's standard process for placing data on legal hold and delivering immutable log exports for litigation? Specifically we need:

- Which log types can be frozen/exported (audit/timestamps, request/response bodies, system events, admin actions)
- Expected timelines to produce a defensible export once a hold is issued
- Chain-of-custody/verification steps (hashing, signature, tamper-evidence)
- Supported export formats and compression
- Delivery methods (S3 presigned, encrypted courier, direct transfer)
- Any required approvals from Redwood or constraints for tenant-scoped vs global logs

We also ask that any standard artifacts (manifest, checklist) be attached or referenced. Our legal team will use this to evaluate preservation SLAs.

Thanks,

Hi Sandra — thanks for the clear list. I've summarized our standard preservation and handoff playbook below and attached two supporting artifacts (matrix + manifest). Laura and Marcus are looped for technical confirmation.

Quick summary (high level):
- Scope: We can place both tenant-scoped and account-level audit trails on hold. Scope is configurable per preservation request; tenant-scoped preservation isolates exports to the customer/tenant ID provided.
- Types preserved: request/response logs (timestamped), admin activity, system audit events (authn/authorization), configuration snapshots, and retention-change audit records. We do not capture ephemeral KV cache contents for inference execution unless explicitly configured as part of a forensic extraction.
- Timeline: preliminary immutable snapshot (hash + manifest) within 48–72 hours of an approved legal hold; full export (compressed, integrity-checked) delivered within 5 business days for standard volumes. For very large datasets we provide a staggered delivery schedule and prioritize a manifest + hashes first.
- Chain-of-custody & verification: every snapshot includes a CSV manifest, SHA256 checksums for each file, and a signed delivery statement from Redwood security. Manifests are stored with time-stamped, write-once metadata.
- Formats & delivery: gzipped JSONL (default) or Parquet upon request; archives are PGP-encrypted for transfer. Delivery methods: AWS S3 presigned URL (time-limited), direct SFTP to customer-provided host, or encrypted physical transfer in exceptional cases.
- Approvals & constraints: legal hold requests must come from an authorized Acme contact (we'll validate against an approved contact list). For tenant-scoped exports, we require tenant identifier + time range. Global/system logs may include cross-tenant metadata — export scoping discussion will be part of the intake.

Attachments included: legal-preservation-matrix.xlsx (matrix mapping log types to retention/format/ownership) and log-extract-manifest.csv (sample manifest layout).

Kimberly — appreciate the detail. A few clarifying questions from our side before we include this in the RFP response packet:

1) Can you preserve per-tenant request/response payloads that contain PII without redaction, or do you require redaction for exports? If redaction is default, can you attest to reversible redaction under court order?
2) Do exports include developer-level debug traces or only production request logs? We need to understand whether debug-level traces (which may contain secrets) are captured and how they are excluded.
3) Supported export formats: you mentioned JSONL and Parquet. For our eDiscovery process we prefer Parquet with typed fields. Is there a size or cost delta we should expect?
4) What is the maximum realistic SLA for full export for a single tenant up to 5 TB? 5 business days is fine for smaller datasets but please call out constraints.
5) Are exported archives accompanied by an auditable access log showing who accessed the exported files and when (Redwood's side and customer's side)?

This is fairly time-sensitive as we aim to freeze the RFP answers by end of month. If needed, we can accept your standard response and note open items as 'to be negotiated'.

Thanks,

Sandra

Hi Sandra — answers below, aligned to your numbered list. Laura and Marcus validated the technical notes.

1) PII & redaction: Redwood preserves raw request/response payloads for tenant-scoped legal holds by default (no automatic redaction) if the customer explicitly requests preservation of raw payloads. Redaction is configurable as part of the intake: we support reversible redaction (cryptographic wrapping) that allows recovery under court order provided appropriate legal controls are in place. We require a written request from an authorized Acme legal contact to preserve unredacted payloads.

2) Debug traces & developer logs: production request/response logs and system audit trails are included in standard exports. Developer/debug-level tracing (verbose SDK logs, ephemeral debug dumps) are retained separately and are excluded from standard legal exports unless specifically requested and authorized through the incident/forensics intake process. Any inclusion of debug traces will be documented in the manifest with explicit owner and justification.

3) Export formats & costs: we support gzipped JSONL (default) and Parquet (columnar, preferred for large-scale analytics). Parquet exports incur additional processing time for schema enforcement and typing; for typical workloads expect a 10–20% processing uplift on export time and related data egress costs based on compressed size. We can provide a cost estimate once we know data volume.

4) SLA for large exports (example: single tenant up to 5 TB): standard timeline is up to 5 business days for typical volumes (under ~500GB). For volumes up to 5 TB we publish a 7–10 business day target and provide provisional staggered delivery. Extremely large or highly sharded datasets may extend beyond that and are handled as a scoped professional-services engagement with defined milestones.

5) Access logging: yes — every delivered archive includes a Redwood audit log for the export operation (who requested, timestamps, manifest, delivery URL). We also produce an integrity log recording access events on our side (who downloaded the file from Redwood storage). If you need cross-organization audit linking we can provide signed access receipts as part of the handoff.

Operational notes:
- Preservation is enacted via a hold ticket in our case management system; once enacted, standard retention/TTL rules are disabled for the affected tenant/time-range.
- We sign manifests with SHA256 and provide a signed delivery statement (PKI-backed).
- For court proceedings we recommend early scoping to agree on format and delivery to avoid delays during the discovery window.

Sample artifacts: link to sample export (private share): https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/sample-export-ACME-202611 (requires shared access).

If this resolves your open items we can include these bullets in the RFP response packet and mark any high-volume export SLA as 'negotiable/PS engagement' per our standard template. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if your legal or eDiscovery team wants a walkthrough.
